=== 00010000 [PLATE]
Trap at the first byte of the loaded image: INT3 to break into a debugger, then JMP back to itself, so control that lands on offset 0 halts there instead of running on into the code that follows.
Pool: crt  [CLIB3S.LIB(cstrt386), BEGTEXT segment head - byte-exact library match]
Evidence: cc eb fd followed by thirteen 90 bytes occurs exactly once in Watcom 10.0a LIB386/DOS/CLIB3S.LIB, at file offset 0x452c, directly after the PUBDEF block naming ___begtext, __nullarea, _cstart_, __exit, __do_exit_with_msg__ and __GETDS - the startup module cstrt386, as its BEGTEXT LEDATA content. The image holds those same 16 bytes here. Not binary_artifact: shipped inside a library object, not synthesised by this link, so it comes back by linking CLIB3S. Not fdps: no game data, strings or callers; game code starts at 00010010 where _TEXT begins. Not ail: nothing AIL-side reaches it. The five DATA xrefs are the constant 0x10000 mis-read as an address; the only true reference is its own backward jump.
Name: no library symbol identified - cstrt386 places ___begtext at offset 3, immediately after these bytes, so the trap carries no symbol of its own, and 3 bytes are too few for Function ID.
Boundary: 00010000-00010002, the INT3 plus the unconditional self-JMP are the whole body; the 13 trailing 90 bytes are BEGTEXT alignment padding, already defined as data and labelled ___begtext at 00010003.
Signature: no convention is exercised - no argument is read, no frame built, and the self-JMP means it never returns. Ghidra's __watcall void(void) is its guess, unconfirmed, and left as is because it is vacuously true here.

=== 00010001 [EOL]
JMP self (eb fd) inside the Watcom CRT trap stub at 00010000: bytes 2-3 of the BEGTEXT segment of cstrt386.obj (CLIB3S), not a function entry and not linker fill

=== 00010003 [EOL]

=== 00010010 [PLATE]
Advance a single battle-map actor one behavior step, dispatching on the low nibble of unit record byte 0x34.
Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_unit_record / fdps_battle_move_unit_toward / fdps_play_sfx and touches game globals; no Function ID hit in either library set]
Evidence: References game-defined symbols and data (unit record array DAT_00069cd8 with 0x50-byte stride, DAT_0006013c, DAT_000640d8, DAT_00063f78/88/8c, DAT_00069cd0, strings "Chess.wav" and "Posion.saf"), which a separately compiled vendor object could not do. Called from fdps_title_demo and three other game dispatchers. Function ID matched nothing in the Watcom 10.0x libraries or in ailv3.lib, and at 1861 bytes with a 12-way state switch it is not linker-emitted glue, so crt, ail and binary_artifact are all excluded.
Name: Game code, so fdps_ + snake_case; no vendor symbol involved.
Boundary: 00010010-00010754, Watcom prologue 53 56 57 55 89 e5 / SUB ESP,0x4c at the entry and the matching MOV ESP,EBP / POP EBP,EDI,ESI,EBX / RET at the end; the 11 bytes after it are Watcom alignment padding (LEA EAX,[EAX+0] / LEA EDX,[EDX+0] / MOV EBX,EBX) up to the separate function FUN_00010760, which this body itself calls at 0001067e.
Signature: __cdecl, void (int actor_index, int context); both arguments read from [EBP+0x14] and [EBP+0x18], plain RET with caller cleanup, no value returned. Confirmed by the assembly, not a guess.

Algorithm:
Resolves the actor record for the given index through fdps_get_unit_record (0002d210); the same record is reachable as DAT_00069cd8 + index * 0x50, confirming the 0x50-byte stride. If bit 0 of record[5] is set the actor is inactive and the function returns immediately.

Otherwise it reads the behavior mode from the low nibble of record[0x34] plus record[0x35] / record[0x36] (a destination pair) and an event slot index in record[0x3d], and dispatches:
  mode 0, 1, 2  -- try the movement handlers 00012c10 / 000126b0 / 000127c0 / 00012230 in a fixed per-mode order and fall back to 000120d0 when every attempt fails.
  mode 3, 9     -- when 00012c10 does not claim the actor, query 0002dc20 for a target; if one exists move toward its x/y with fdps_battle_move_unit_toward (mode 3 also clears DAT_00069cd0, mode 9 first calls 0002da50), otherwise take the same handler-chain fallback.
  mode 4, 7     -- clear DAT_00069cd0, call 0002da50 and walk toward the record[0x35]/record[0x36] destination. Mode 7, on arrival, plays the "Posion.saf" effect through 00026e00 when record[7] lies in 0x24..0x27, then sets bit 0 of record[5] to retire the actor.
  mode 5         -- event step: if the per-slot flag (&DAT_000640d8)[record[0x3d]] is still clear and 00013e10 yields a destination, walk there; on arrival read the 3-byte entry at DAT_0006013c + slot * 3 + 0x53, copy it into record[0x31]/record[0x32], call 00025d20 when the first byte is zero, set the slot flag, call fdps_map_apply_triggered_cell_changes, switch the actor to mode 7 and play "Chess.wav" through fdps_play_sfx.
  mode 8         -- no action, returns immediately.
  mode 10, 11   -- the driven modes: 00013040 or 00013420, gated extra handlers 00027180 / 00013c90 when DAT_00063f8c / DAT_00063f88 reach 6, then 00012230, and finally 00012e50 or the 000126b0 / 000120d0 fallback depending on DAT_00063f78. Mode 11 additionally invokes FUN_00010760 when record[7] is in 0x3c..0x3e.

After dispatch it re-reads the record, calls 0002e030 with the actor's current x/y and 1, sets bit 0x80 of record[5] to mark the actor for redraw, and calls fdps_render_view_frame.

Parameters:
  actor_index -- index into the actor record array at DAT_00069cd8 (0x50 bytes per record).
  context     -- second stack argument, passed unchanged to every movement handler.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Algorithm:
1. fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) supplies tile x at +0x00, tile y at +0x01, a class index at +0x20 and a movement/terrain cost selector at +0x3b.
2. fdps_get_class_record(class_index + 1) yields the movement context; malloc(100) is the step buffer (one direction code per step) and malloc(0x800) is the reachable-tile list (x,y byte pairs).
3. Build the movement cost map (FUN_00010b90(map_mode) then FUN_00010de0(ctx, x, y, cost_selector)) and path from the unit to (dest_x, dest_y) with fdps_move_path_trace(x, y, step_buf, dest_x, dest_y, 0), which returns the step count or -1 for no path.
4. On failure, retry with the relaxed flag 1. If a relaxed path exists, replay it step by step (direction 0 = y+1, 1 = x-1, 2 = y-1, else x+1), probing each tile with fdps_map_load_tile_info(x, y) and reading DAT_00069d0c. The last tile whose probe is not 0xff becomes the new destination - the request is retargeted to the furthest usable tile along the blocked route.
5. Rebuild the movement map, flood the unit's reach with FUN_000118f0(unit_index, map_mode), and collect the reachable tiles with FUN_00011da0(tile_buf), which returns their count.
6. Scan those tiles and keep the one minimising |tx - dest_x| + |ty - dest_y|, breaking ties on the smaller ||dx| - |dy||.
7. Path to the chosen tile with the strict flag 0. If the step count is non-zero, fdps_animate_move_path(unit_index, step_buf, step_count) performs the move and the result is 1; otherwise 0.
8. Free both buffers and return.

=== 00016300 [PLATE]
Draws the body of the unit status panel for one unit.

Algorithm:
1. If the global mode flag at 0x00060070 is set, latch the caller-supplied unit index into 0x00063fb0.
2. Resolve the unit record via the accessor at 0x0002d210(unit_index) and copy the fields it will print into locals: current/max HP (record+0x40 / +0x42), current/max MP (record+0x44 / +0x46), a two-digit value at +0x21, four three-digit stats at +0x48, +0x4a, +0x4c, +0x4e, a three-digit value at +0x3e, a two-digit value at +0x3b, and byte fields +0x07, +0x08, +0x1f, +0x20 used as sprite indices. Algorithm:
Copies a 15-entry sprite row table from 0x14818 (15, 30, 70, 105, 140, 170, 150, 130, 150, 170, 160, 165, 165, 160, 170 -- a drop from the top of the screen followed by two bounces) into a local array and sets the idle-animation frame counter to -1 (inactive). When allow_idle_animation is non-zero it calls rand and, when the value is a multiple of 200, arms the idle animation by setting the frame counter to 0.

It then loops: poll the input source at 0x178f0; a returned code greater than 0x7f means nothing has been selected yet, so a frame is drawn. The frame is skipped entirely unless the global tick at 0x69d64 differs from the last-drawn tick at 0x63fc0.

Per frame: allocate a 0x15180-byte backing buffer and a 0xfa00-byte 320x200 work buffer, zero the work buffer, capture the current screen into the backing buffer (from 0xa0504 when the mode flag at 0x60070 is set, otherwise via 0x2bf60), copy it back into the work buffer, then free the backing buffer. The walk-cycle frame index is (tick at 0x63fc0 % 16) / 4 with 3 folded back to 1, giving the 0,1,2,1 cycle; it indexes the 0x30-byte per-unit record at the table based at 0x60138, whose four 0x0c-byte groups (offsets 0x00, 0x0c, 0x18, 0x24) hold the four facings, and each stored value is an offset added back to 0x60138 to form the sprite pointer. A 0x240-byte 24x24 scratch buffer receives the decoded cel, is blitted into window_image at offset 0xd21 (row 10, column 161), and window_image is then blitted into the work buffer as a 0x123 x 0xc8 region at offset 0xf.

When the idle animation is armed the frame counter drives four phases: frames 0..14 draw the facing at offset 0x00 at the table's row positions (the drop and the bounces); frames 15..24 draw that same facing standing at row 170, column 161; frames 25..34 draw the facing at offset 0x24 and frames 35..44 the facing at offset 0x0c, both at the same standing position. After frame 44 a separate row counter starting at 170 draws the facing at offset 0x18 walking upward in steps of 4 until it passes row 10, at which point the frame counter returns to -1 and the sprite reverts to the plain walk cycle.

The work buffer is presented to VGA memory at 0xa0000 (whole 64000-byte copy when the mode flag is clear, otherwise a 0x138 x 0xc0 rect blit at 0xa0504), both remaining buffers are freed, and the last-drawn tick is updated.

Parameters:
  window_image -- pointer to the 320-pitch composed status window image; the unit sprite is stamped into it at offset 0xd21 each frame

  allow_idle_animation -- non-zero enables the randomly triggered drop/bounce/turn/rise idle sequence

Returns:
  The input code returned by the poller at 0x178f0 once it is <= 0x7f.

Algorithm:
1. Allocates a 0x561E byte buffer and copies a 302x73 (0x12E x 0x49) region of
   VGA memory at 0xA9609 into it at stride 302. The caller has already drawn the
   prompt panel there, so this captures the panel bitmap. The four corner pixels
   (offsets 0, 0x12D, 0x54F0, 0x561D) are then cleared to 0 so the later masked
   blit renders the panel with transparent (rounded) corners.
2. Loops until a confirm or cancel key arrives. Each iteration:
   - calls fdps_cycle_scene_palette and allocates a 0x15180 byte (360x240)
     off-screen work buffer;
   - if the flag at 00060070 is zero, hands the work buffer to
     fdps_draw_scene_layers to draw the background; otherwise copies the current
     312x192 screen area at 0xA0504 into the work buffer at offset 0x21D8

     x=275, y=123. The unselected side uses a fixed cel (13 for the right slot,
     8 for the left); the selected side cycles a 4-frame animation, cels 4..7 on
     the left and 9..12 on the right, indexed by ((frame/3)%4);
   - waits for vertical retrace by polling port 0x3DA (bit 3 set, then clear),
     blits the work buffer back to the screen at 0xA0504 (312x192), spins until
     the tick counter at 00069D64 changes, records it as the animation frame,
     and frees the work buffer;
   - reads a scancode via 000567BE: 0x1C (Enter) or 0x39 (Space) confirms and
     keeps the current selection; 0x01 (Esc) or 0x53 (Del) exits with -1;

3. Frees the captured panel buffer and returns the selection.

Selection starts at 0, so the left option is highlighted on entry.

Parameters: none.

Returns: 0 or 1 for the confirmed option (left or right), -1 if cancelled.

Algorithm:
1. Clears the input-enabled flag at 0x00060159, allocates a 0x15180-byte offscreen map buffer with malloc and renders the battle map into it with fdps_draw_scene_layers.
2. Walks every unit (count at 0x00060150, record via fdps_get_unit_record). A unit whose kind byte +0x06 == 2, with none of bits 0x81 set in byte +0x05, zero in bytes +0x25 and +0x26, and current HP (+0x40) differing from max HP (+0x42) recovers maxHP/5 HP clamped to max. 3. Waits for the VGA vertical retrace by polling port 0x3DA bit 3 (inp), then blits the map viewport from buffer+0x21d8 to 0xa0504 with fdps_blit_rect. If any unit rested, plays REST.WAV through fdps_play_sfx. Delays 40 ticks, frees the buffer and repaints with fdps_render_view_frame.
4. Selects side 1 (0x0002e0c0 / 0x0001fa30) and runs 0x00012b20.
5. Shows the EnyPhase.saf banner, clears status bit 7 on all units, selects side 0 and runs 0x00012960; restarts the CD battle track first.
6. Increments the turn counter at 0x00069ce8, shows the PlyPhase.saf banner, clears 0x00069cd0, replays the CD track and selects side 2.
7. Applies per-unit MP regeneration: looks up 0xa6 then 0xa7 on unit 4, 0xb1 on unit 8, and 0xb3 on every unit via 0x00034520. When the found slot has bit 0x40 set in unit+0x0a[slot], byte +0x05 is zero and current MP (+0x44) differs from max MP (+0x46), the unit gains MP via 0x000275a0(unit, 0x0f), the view scrolls to it (0x0002da50), a type-0x0d floating value is shown (0x0001f510) and the display is waited on (0x0001f340).
8. Sets 0x00069cd0 = 1, centres the view on unit 0 unless 0x000109b0 says otherwise, calls 0x000567b3 and re-enables input at 0x00060159.

Every stage from step 4 on is guarded by the battle-abort flag at 0x00069da0; when it is non-zero the function returns immediately without re-enabling input.

Signature: __cdecl, uchar *(char *bg_cel_name) - the sole argument is read from [EBP+0x14], no register arguments are read, and cleanup is the caller's on every call including this one.

Algorithm:
1. Loads the background cel named by bg_cel_name out of MISC.VFS, allocates a 0xfa00-byte page, blits the cel into it at pitch 0x140 with all clip/offset arguments zero, then frees the cel.
2. Allocates a 0x59cb-byte save buffer and opens FDE.SAV with the mode string at 0x61a00. If the file exists it is read whole (fread size 1, count 0x59cb), XOR-decrypted over the same 0x59cb bytes and closed; otherwise the buffer is filled with 0xFF so every slot reads as empty.
3. For each of the three slots i (record base = buf + 0x312b + i * 0xa28) the byte at record + 0xa00 is the occupied marker: 0xFF stores 0 into the slot-occupied array at 0x640f8[i], anything else stores 1. The record is then drawn by FUN_00024a40 into the page at row 0x1a + i * 0x34, column 0x0d, pitch 0x140. The save buffer is freed afterwards.
4. If the flag at 0x69cf0 is set, the previously loaded icon block at 0x60138 is freed and the flag cleared. ICON.CEL is then opened and, for each of the 0x64114 party records (array at 0x64108, stride 0x50), the icon id at record + 7 is passed to fdps_cache_cel_sprite_group together with the open file; the file is closed at the end.
5. Returns the offscreen page. Ownership passes to the caller, which frees it.

Algorithm:
  1. access("DISK.NO", 0). A non-zero result means the game was never installed: print the two error strings at 00061be8 and "Please use install function.", then exit(1).
  2. fopen("Disk.no", format at 00061c2c), three fscanf(fp, "%s", ...) reads and fclose(). The first two tokens go to the stack buffer at [EBP-0x1c] and are discarded; the third is stored in the global string buffer at 000643e8. Sets 00069d54 to -1.

  5.   6. Shutdown: fdps_shutdown_free_resources(), fdps_audio_shutdown(), fdps_cd_stop_audio(), int386(0x10, &regs, &regs) with regs.ax = 3 to return to text mode, and finally prints "\nThank you for playing Flame Dragon Plus!! \n\n".

=== 0002a2b0 [PLATE]
Title screen and opening attract loop; the only caller is main.

Algorithm:
1. Reset the input/keyboard state (FUN_000567b3), set the global 'in title screen' flag at 0x60159 and clear 0x64110.
2. Try to open the save file "FDE.SAV", read 0x59cb bytes into a malloc'd buffer, close it, decrypt it with fdps_xor_crypt_buffer, then compute a checksum over the buffer (FUN_00056898) and compare it against the dword at buffer+0x59c7. If the checksum matches and the byte at buffer+0x30c5 is not 0xff, clear menu-state entries 1 and 2 of the local 4-byte menu flag array (initialised from the dword at 0x29210, where 0 means selectable and non-zero means greyed out), i.e. enable the save-dependent menu entries.
3. Outer attract loop, repeated until a menu entry has been chosen: load "Dynasty.pal" from MISC.VFS, allocate a 0x16480 byte animation buffer and load "Logo.saf"; play the animation frame by frame with fdps_saf_advance_tick, blitting the frame at offset 0x2298 to 0xa0000 (320x200, source pitch 0x170) after waiting on the VGA vertical retrace bit of port 0x3da and on the timer tick counter at 0x69d64. Any key with scancode < 0x80 aborts the animation.
4. Format "FD%d" with the alternating index at local_18+1 and play that opening movie with fdps_play_movie, set the flag at 0x60008 and call FUN_00030bf0(1). Then enter the title menu loop: load "StSel.cel", "StBoard.cel" and "StBoard.pal" from MISC.VFS, allocate a 64000 byte offscreen buffer, and run a menu frame loop with a 0x6d6 tick idle counter. Up (0x48) and Down (0x50) move the selection modulo 4; Enter (0x1c) or Space (0x39) accepts, but only when the selected entry's flag byte is 0. Each frame clears the offscreen buffer, draws the board cel, draws the four selection cels using frame index i*3 + (i == selection ? 1 : flags[i]) at y = 0x48 + i*0x11, waits for retrace and copies the buffer to 0xa0000.
5. On exit from the menu loop, fade the palette to black over 10 retrace-synchronised steps, clear video memory, free all buffers and restore the palette from 0x643bc. If the idle counter did not reach zero, dispatch on the selection: 0 starts a new game through the state-machine function pointer table at 0x60074 (index 0x69cf4), 1 allocates a 64000 byte buffer and opens fdps_load_game_screen, running fdps_run_village_phase when it returns 1, 2 calls fdps_load_savegame, and 3 sets the flag at 0x643eb; every branch then sets 0x69cd0 to 1. If the idle counter did reach zero, fdps_title_demo runs instead and the whole cycle repeats with the other movie index.

Parameters: none.

Returns: the index of the title menu entry that was finally chosen (0-3).

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; calls the game's own subsystems]
Evidence: Called only by main@00029220 and calls fdps_vfs_load_entry, fdps_play_movie, fdps_saf_advance_tick, fdps_cel_blit_sprite, fdps_set_palette_range, fdps_load_savegame, fdps_load_game_screen and fdps_run_village_phase - link direction rules out a third-party compiled object, so neither crt nor ail. Name: game-pool function named descriptively under the fdps_ rule; no vendor symbol is involved and no Function ID candidate exists, so the name cannot be a shape collision.

Builds the game's palette lookup tables from a 256-entry VGA palette: packs each entry into a nibble-per-channel RGB word at 000657f0, scales that row by 16 brightness coefficients into 000653f0, and fills a 16x16x16 RGB-to-palette-index cube at 000643f0.
Pool: fdps  [no library match; game-owned globals and call graph]
Evidence: Called only by fdps_load_global_resources and calls fdps_palette_find_nearest_color plus three local component extractors (0002ae90/0002aec0/0002aef0); writes the game tables 000643f0, 000653f0 and 000657f0 and reads the 18-dword coefficient table at 0002ae40. Function ID finds no match in the Watcom or ail sets and the hash is unique in the image; no CRT or AIL entry point, no driver state, and far too large for a linker artifact.
Name: fdps_ + snake_case describing what the body builds; no vendor symbol involved.
Boundary: 0002af60-0002b1a3, Watcom prologue 53 56 57 55 89 e5 to the matching MOV ESP,EBP/POP/RET epilogue; the 12 bytes after it are LEA-form alignment padding before fdps_palette_find_nearest_color at 0002b1b0.
Signature: __cdecl, void fdps_build_palette_tables(uchar *palette) -- the single argument is read from [EBP+0x14], the RET purges nothing, and the calls it makes clean up with ADD ESP,n.
Algorithm:
1. Copies the 18-dword brightness coefficient table at 0002ae40 onto the stack, indexed by shade level.
2. For each of the 256 palette entries: reads the three bytes (r,g,b) of the source palette (6-bit VGA components, scaled by 4 to 8 bits), packs them as r<<16|g<<8|b, then calls the three component extractors. Each result is masked with 0xF0 and repositioned so red lands in bits 16-19, green in bits 8-11 and blue in bits 0-3. Row 0 of the ramp table (000653f0) is zeroed and the packed value is stored into row 1 (000657f0 = 000653f0 + 0x400).
3. For levels 2..17, each of the 256 row-1 values is multiplied by the level coefficient and stored at 000653f0[level*256 + index]. Because each channel occupies only the low nibble of its own byte, one multiply scales all three channels without carrying between them.
4. Fills the 16x16x16 inverse lookup cube at 000643f0: for every (r,g,b) triple of 4-bit components (passed as component*4) it calls fdps_palette_find_nearest_color with the source palette and stores the returned index as a byte, written sequentially over 4096 entries.

=== 0002b1b0 [PLATE]
Returns the index of the palette entry closest to a target colour, by minimum squared RGB distance over a 256-entry, 3-bytes-per-entry table.
Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; unique hash in the image; called only by game graphics code]
Evidence: fid.watcom and fid.ail are both empty and same_hash_in_image is 1, so there is no library byte match. Its only reference is a static call from fdps_build_palette_tables@0002af60, which writes the returned index into the game's 16x16x16 colour lookup table at DAT_000643f0. Nearest-colour matching is not a CLIB3S/MATH387S/EMU387 or Miles AIL service, and 202 bytes of real loop logic cannot be a linker thunk or merged epilogue.
Name: game code, so fdps_ + snake_case describing the algorithm; no vendor symbol claimed or available.
Boundary: 0002b1b0-0002b279, Watcom prologue 53 56 57 55 89 e5 at the call target through the matching MOV ESP,EBP / POP EBP,EDI,ESI,EBX / RET; no body holes, and the gap after 0002b27a is defined data with no instructions.
Signature: __cdecl, int (int r, int g, int b, uchar *palette). Arguments are read from [EBP+0x14/0x18/0x1c/0x20], RET takes no immediate, and the caller cleans with ADD ESP,0x10; result in EAX.
Algorithm: best distance seeded with 10000000 and best index with 0x100, then 256 fixed iterations over an advancing byte cursor forming dr = r - pal[0], dg = g - pal[1], db = b - pal[2] and dr*dr + dg*dg + db*db in signed 32-bit arithmetic. The strict less-than test makes the first of several equally close entries win. The palette buffer must therefore hold at least 768 bytes. The palette bytes are zero-extended but the target components are not masked, so the caller is responsible for keeping r/g/b in range; with in-range targets the 0x100 seed can never survive and the result is always 0..255.

Algorithm:
Obtains the shared keyboard-state byte via the low-level key accessor FUN_00056799 and primes it to 0xFF. Reads map dimensions from the header pointed to by DAT_00060144 (word 0 = width, word 1 = height) and converts both to pixel extents by multiplying by the 24-pixel tile size. Then loops until the local exit flag becomes non-zero.

Each iteration polls input (fdps_cd_music_repeat_poll), reads the current scancode and maintains an auto-repeat counter: the same scancode as last time increments it, a different one resets it and records the new code. The full dispatch runs only when the counter is 0 (first press) or greater than 5 (auto-repeat engaged); while it is 1..5 control goes to the reduced path that handles F1 and F2/Home only.

Scancode dispatch:
  0x48/0x50 (up/down)     move cursor Y at DAT_00069ccc by one tile, clamped to map height
  0x4B/0x4D (left/right)  move cursor X at DAT_00069cd4 by one tile, clamped to map width
                          each accepted move calls fdps_play_sfx("Beep.wav")
  0x01/0x2C/0x4C/0x53     cycle forward through the unit table: from the saved rotation index, scan up to
                          DAT_00060150 records of 0x50 bytes based at DAT_00069cd8 and stop at the first with
                          (flags[+5] & 0x85) == 0 and side[+6] == 2, centre on it via fdps_map_cursor_move_to
                          with its tile coordinates scaled by 24, and save the next index
  0x1C/0x39 (Enter/Space) clear the key latch (FUN_000567b3), resolve the unit under the cursor
                          (fdps_battle_find_unit_at_cursor); with no unit, open fdps_battle_system_menu and take
                          its return as the exit flag; with a unit that is friendly (side[+6] == 2), not marked
                          done (flags[+5] & 0x80) and with byte +0x26 clear, run fdps_battle_unit_turn and then,
                          if DAT_00069da0 is still clear, fdps_battle_end_phase_if_all_units_done; otherwise show
                          fdps_battle_show_unit_status_window
  0x3B (F1)               fdps_battle_map_overview
  0x3C/0x47 (F2/Home)     resolve the unit under the cursor and show its status window

After dispatch the camera origin (X at DAT_00069ce4, Y at DAT_00069ce0) scrolls by one tile whenever the cursor comes within one tile of a viewport edge, clamped so the 0x138 by 0xC0 pixel viewport stays inside the map. The frame is drawn by fdps_render_view_frame, and the loop exits once DAT_00069da0 is non-zero.

None. Any decompiler param_1/param_2/unaff_EBX are artifacts; no incoming stack slot or register is read before being written.

Nothing.

=== 0002df90 [PLATE]
Re-seats the unit-record table at 0x00069cd8 into a freshly allocated block at a randomised heap address, wiping the old copy: it mallocs a rand()%0x400+1 scratch block and holds it across the table allocation so the new block lands at a varying offset, mallocs (DAT_00060150 + 1) * 0x50 bytes, memmoves that full length out of the old block, memsets the old block to zero over its own length, frees the old block and then the scratch block, and stores the new pointer into 0x00069cd8. The entry count is never modified, so this does not grow the table.
Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either library; hash unique in the image]
Evidence: All three callers are settled game code -- fdps_battle_unit_turn@00015470 and the two per-side battle sweeps FUN_00012960 and FUN_00012b20, whose plates name this address as the routine they run at the top of every unit iteration. It consumes the runtime as a client, pushing arguments and cleaning the stack for malloc/memmove/memset/free/rand. The body is entirely bookkeeping over two FDPS globals (count 0x00060150, array pointer 0x00069cd8) with a hard-coded 0x50-byte stride, the same pair owned by fdps_get_unit_record@0002d210 and allocated by 00022be0 and 000232b0; no AIL state area, driver structure or library string data, and far too large and stateful for a linker island or convention shim.
Name: no library symbol identified; fdps code, left as FUN_ for the later naming ticket.
Boundary: 0002df90-0002e02c, Watcom prologue 53 56 57 55 89 e5 at the entry, matching epilogue and RET at 0002e02c, then 3 bytes of 8d 40 00 alignment padding before the next prologue at 0002e030.
Signature: __cdecl, void FUN_0002df90(void) -- nothing is read from a register before it is written or from the argument slot at [EBP+0x14] and up, and RET purges 0; all three call sites are bare CALLs with nothing pushed, no ADD ESP after, and EAX reloaded from a local on the very next instruction, so the pointer left in EAX is not a return value (it is published through the global instead). The prologue is the canonical -4s stack-convention form and every callee is called stack-style with caller cleanup (CLIB3S); with zero parameters __cdecl and __watcall are byte-identical, so Ghidra's __watcall was an unconfirmed guess rather than a contradiction.

Algorithm:
1. scratch = malloc(rand() % 0x400 + 1). Signed IDIV by 0x400 with SAR EDX,0x1f, so the size is 1..0x400 for a non-negative rand() and can be 0x400 down to -0x3ff+1 only if rand() were negative, which Watcom's rand never returns.
2. new_size = (DAT_00060150 + 1) * 0x50; block = malloc(new_size). The scratch block is still held, so this allocation is displaced by a random amount.
3. memmove(block, DAT_00069cd8, new_size) -- see the over-read note below.
4. memset(DAT_00069cd8, 0, new_size - 0x50), i.e. the OLD block over exactly its own length, then free(DAT_00069cd8), then free(scratch).
5. DAT_00069cd8 = block. DAT_00060150 is untouched.

Table size invariant and the over-read: the live table is exactly DAT_00060150 * 0x50 bytes. 00022be0 sets DAT_00060150 from DAT_00064118 and mallocs DAT_00064118 * 0x50; 000232b0 mallocs 0x50 when the count is 0 and otherwise reallocs to (count + 1) * 0x50, and only then increments the count. So the block this routine allocates is one record LONGER than the source it copies from, and the memmove reads 0x50 bytes past the end of the old allocation to fill the spare tail slot with heap garbage. That slot is never live data (the count does not change), so the over-read is harmless in practice, but it is original behaviour and must be reproduced verbatim -- copying only count * 0x50 would be a 'fix' that changes the emitted code.

Why it exists: the two mechanisms only make sense together. Holding a randomly sized scratch block across the allocation moves the table to a different heap address on every call, and zeroing the old block immediately before returning it to the heap destroys the stale copy. The routine is invoked once per unit at the top of each battle sweep, so the unit records never sit still at one address for long -- this is a deliberate defence against memory scanners and trainers, not a resize.

The horizontal bound test compares a block-column index against the pixel width while the vertical one compares a pixel row against the pixel height, so the horizontal test is far looser; the real horizontal bound is the blocks_x loop count. === 00030010 [PLATE]
Alpha-blends a single constant palette colour over an 8bpp source rectangle, resolving each blended colour back to a palette index through an inverse-palette table.
Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit on either library set; hash unique in the image; called only from named game code]
Evidence: fid.watcom and fid.ail are both empty with zero candidates, and full_hash aa05da20779be6da has same_hash_in_image 1 and same_hash_in_ail_lib 0, so these bytes match nothing in CLIB3S/MATH387S/EMU387 or ailv3.lib. The only references are three static calls from fdps_play_vfs_animation and fdps_show_game_over - no function-pointer table slot, so no other module decides the pool. It calls nothing and touches no globals, no AIL state and no DOS state. The arithmetic is game-specific 8bpp palette compositing against the game's own weighted blend table and inverse-palette LUT, which is no C runtime service, and at 262 bytes with a full frame and two nested loops it is far larger than anything the linker or compiler emits, so not binary_artifact.
Name: fdps_ + snake_case for game code; no vendor symbol to collide with, and the unique hash rules out a shape collision.
Boundary: 00030010-00030115, entry on the Watcom prologue 53 56 57 55 89 e5 / sub esp,0x1c whose four pushes explain the first argument sitting at [EBP+0x14], end on the RET closing the matching epilogue; the 10 bytes after it are LEA-form NOP padding aligning the next function to 00030120.
Signature: __cdecl, confirmed by the assembly - all ten arguments are read from [EBP+0x14] through [EBP+0x38], EAX/EDX/EBX/ECX are written before ever being read so nothing arrives in registers, and the plain RET leaves the caller to clean up. Returns nothing.

Algorithm:
blend_table is a [18][256] array of dwords holding each palette entry pre-scaled by a weight, with the three colour channels packed one per byte (channel n in bits 8n+4..8n+7 before the shift below). Rows 0..8 hold weights 0..8; rows 9..17 (dword offset 0x900 = 9*256) hold the complementary weights. To keep the row index inside 0..8 the function folds alpha: for alpha <= 8 the constant colour reads row alpha and the source pixels read row 9+alpha; for alpha > 8 alpha is replaced by 16-alpha, the constant colour reads row 9+alpha' and the source pixels read row alpha'. Either way the constant colour ends up weighted by the caller's alpha and the source pixel by 16-alpha.
The scaled constant colour is fetched once before the loops. For each pixel the scaled source colour is added to it, the sum is shifted right by 4 (dividing out the /16 of the weights) and masked with 0x000F0F0F, leaving 4 bits per channel at bits 0..3, 8..11 and 16..19. Those are folded into a 12-bit index by (v & 0xFFFF) | (v >> 12), giving channel0 in bits 0..3, channel2 in bits 4..7 and channel1 in bits 8..11. That index selects a palette byte from the 4096-entry inverse-palette table rgb444_lut, which is stored to the destination.
Rows advance by src_stride and dst_stride; no clipping, no transparency test, every pixel in the rectangle is written.

Parameters:
src         - source 8bpp pixels, top-left of the rectangle
src_stride  - bytes to add to src per row
dst         - destination 8bpp pixels, top-left of the rectangle
dst_stride  - bytes to add to dst per row
width       - pixels per row
height      - number of rows
blend_table - base of the [18][256] dword weighted-colour table
rgb444_lut  - base of the 4096-entry packed-RGB to palette-index table
tint_color  - palette index of the constant colour being blended in
alpha       - blend weight of tint_color, 0..16 (0 = source only, 16 = tint only)

Returns:
Nothing.

=== 00030cc0 [PLATE]
Waits until the disc required by the given chapter is inserted, then starts that chapter's CD audio track.
Pool: fdps  [game strings, game globals, five named game callers]
Evidence: References "%s\\Pack.vfs" and the VFS entry "Pass.Dat", the game path global at 000643e8 and the draw context at 000643c4; writes the current-track global at 00069d54 that fdps_cd_play_track / fdps_cd_stop_audio use. No Function ID hit in either library set and the body hash is unique in the image, so not crt; no Miles state or AIL caller, so not ail; a full Watcom frame with real control flow, so not binary_artifact.
Name: fdps_ + snake_case describing the behaviour; no vendor symbol involved.
Boundary: 00030cc0-00030f31, ends at the epilogue MOV ESP,EBP / POP EBP,EDI,ESI,EBX / RET; the 14 bytes after it are Watcom alignment padding before the next function at 00030f40.
Signature: __cdecl void (int chapter, int slot) - both arguments read as dwords from [EBP+0x14] and [EBP+0x18], bare RET so the caller cleans; confirmed by the assembly, not a guess.

Algorithm:
1. Copy the 60-byte constant table at 000304a0 onto the stack (15 dwords). It is 30 chapter rows of 2 bytes; the row is the chapter, the column is the slot, and the byte is a zero-based CD audio track index (0xff means no track).
2. Stop any playing CD audio (fdps_cd_stop_audio).
3. Loop until the inserted disc is acceptable:
   - Release the keyboard ISR (FUN_00056818) and drain pending input (kbhit / getch).
   - Format "%s\\Pack.vfs" from the game path global at 000643e8 with sprintf and probe it with access(path, 0). A non-zero result means no usable disc.
   - When the probe succeeds, load the "Pass.Dat" entry through fdps_vfs_load_entry and take its first byte minus '0' as the disc number (1 or 2).
   - Chapters 0..17 live on disc 1, chapters 18 (0x12) and above on disc 2. If the probe failed, or the disc number does not match the chapter, draw the matching prompt through FUN_0001ff60 with the draw context at 000643c4 (message 0x223 for "insert disc 2", 0x222 for "insert disc 1"), wait for a keypress with getch, draw message 0x22a, delay(0x4e20), tear the prompt down (FUN_00020820) and retry from step 2.
   - Otherwise set the done flag and leave the loop.
4. Reinstall the keyboard ISR (fdps_install_keyboard_isr).
5. If the CD audio enable flag at 00060008 is clear, store -1 into the current-track global at 00069d54 and stop CD audio. Otherwise take table[chapter * 2 + slot], store it at 00069d54, and if it is not -1 start playback of that value + 1 (fdps_cd_play_track).

Parameters:
  chapter - chapter index; also selects the required disc (>= 18 means disc 2).
  slot    - which of the chapter's two track entries to use, 0 or 1.

Returns:
  Nothing. Does not return until an acceptable disc is present.

Signature: __cdecl, no arguments (no register or [ESP+n] argument is read, both call sites push nothing), returns the menu selection in EAX, caller cleans up.

Algorithm:
1. Poll the service routine at 0x000567b3, then return 0 immediately if the abort flag at 0x000643eb is set.
2. Test the chapter number at 0x00069cf4. Chapters 0x10, 0x11, 0x15, 0x16 and >0x19 have no village: fade out via 0x00030bf0(-1) and, unless the suppress flag at 0x00060131 is set, clear VGA memory at 0xa0000 (64000 bytes), apply the palette at 0x000643bc via fdps_set_palette_range, then allocate, clear, present via 0x000241e0 and free a 64000-byte offscreen page. Control then jumps to step 6.
3. Otherwise set the in-village flag at 0x00060070, load "ShopWin.Cel" from "MISC.VFS" via fdps_vfs_load_entry, cache the handle in 0x00069d84, call fdps_load_field_chapter_resources and fade in via 0x00030bf0(2).
4. 5. Dispatch selection-1 through the jump table at 0x00031328: 1 -> fdps_run_bar_shop, 2 -> fdps_run_church_screen, 3 -> fdps_village_item_menu, 4 -> fdps_run_weapon_shop, 5 -> fdps_run_secret_menu. After the bar-shop arm this function re-tests the chapter number and forces the selection back to 0 for the chapters that have no village. Poll 0x000567b3 and repeat while the selection is non-zero and no abort is pending; on exit free both cached cel handles and clear 0x00060070, 0x00060150 and 0x00069cd8.
6. Save and clear the input-enable byte at 0x00060158, fade out via 0x00030bf0(-1), and unless an abort is pending call the chapter script taken from the per-chapter function pointer table at 0x00060074 indexed by the chapter number. Restore 0x00060158, clear 0x00060131, and call fdps_cd_verify_disc_and_play_track(chapter, 0).

Returns: the menu selection left when the loop exited, 0 on a normal exit and 0 when the abort flag was already set on entry.

Algorithm:
1. fdps_vfs_find_entry(name, vfs) gives the entry index; on -1 it prints "Can't find the string: %s" and returns NULL.
2. memcpy 13 bytes of the archive path stored at vfs+4 into a local buffer and fopen(path, mode at 0006201c); on failure prints "Can't open the source VFS_file: %s" and returns NULL.
3. Takes the entry byte length from [vfs + index*0x1a + 0x1e] and malloc()s it; on failure prints "Can't allocate memory for VFS_file: %s(%dbytes)", still fcloses the file and returns NULL.
4. Takes the entry file offset from [vfs + index*0x1a + 0x27], fseek(fp, offset, 0), fread(buf, length, 1, fp), fclose(fp).
5. Returns the allocated buffer, which the caller owns.

=== 0003bade [PLATE]
Allocates two 512-byte DOS real-mode buffers via DPMI INT 31h function 0100h and publishes their real-mode segments and flat linear addresses in the CD-ROM/MSCDEX globals.
Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; called only by fdps_cdrom_detect; writes the game's own CD state block]
Evidence: Link direction and shared data. The sole reference to the entry is the call from fdps_cdrom_detect at 0003c698, and its callees are the CRT helpers __CHK, memset and int386x - game code using the runtime, not runtime code. Function ID is empty against both the Watcom 10.0x libraries and ailv3.lib (0 candidates on each), so no vendor module owns these bytes. Every write lands in the 0x00069da4-0x00069e54 CD-ROM state area that fdps_cd_device_request reads; nothing touches CRT or AIL state. It is a full compiled body with a stack probe, so not binary_artifact.
Name: no library symbol identified; fdps_ + snake_case name describing what the body does, consistent with fdps_cdrom_detect and fdps_cd_device_request around it.
Boundary: 0003bade-0003bb7c, PUSH 0x14 / CALL __CHK is the Watcom stack-probe prologue at a real entry, the RET at 0003bb7c ends it, gap_after is empty, and 0003bb7d opens the identical prologue of fdps_cd_device_request.
Signature: void (void), __watcall. No argument register is read before being written and nothing is fetched from the caller's frame; each PUSH group is balanced by the function's own ADD ESP before a plain RET. For a zero-argument void function __watcall and __cdecl are indistinguishable in code, so __watcall is the compilation unit's default rather than a distinction the assembly makes.

Algorithm:
1. memset the 12-byte struct SREGS at 0x00069df0 to zero.
2. Fill the input REGS at 0x00069dc8 with AX = 0x0100 and BX = 0x0020, then call int386x(0x31, in, out, sregs). DPMI 0100h allocates 0x20 paragraphs (512 bytes) of DOS memory below 1MB; the returned AX is the real-mode segment and DX the protected-mode selector, which is discarded.
3. Store the first block's segment as a word at 0x00069e54 and its flat linear address (segment << 4) at 0x00069de8. DOS/4GW identity-maps the first megabyte, so segment << 4 is directly dereferenceable.
4. Repeat the identical DPMI 0100h call for a second 512-byte block; store its segment shifted left 16 bits at 0x00069da8 (a pre-packed seg:0000 real-mode far pointer for the MSCDEX request header's transfer address) and its flat linear address at 0x00069da4.

The input REGS block is not re-initialised before the second call because int386x leaves the caller's input structure untouched.

No error handling: a failed DPMI allocation returns with the carry flag set and garbage in AX, and the resulting addresses are used unchecked by the CD driver functions.

=== 0003bea0 [PLATE]
Pool: fdps

Signature: __watcall void(void). __InitRtns calls it as CALL EAX with no argument register loaded and nothing pushed as an argument -- EAX is the routine pointer itself and EDX is the dispatcher's own priority ceiling, saved across the call because the callee may clobber it -- and the target returns by plain RET with no stack purge, which this JMP inherits. === 00043310 [PLATE]
Watcom C/C++ 10.0a 32-bit DOS startup body: identifies the host DOS extender, shrinks the DOS memory block, copies the PSP command tail and the program name, records the NO87 flag, zeroes BSS, then runs the registered initializers and enters __CMain.
Pool: crt  [cstrt386.obj, _TEXT offset 0x78, from CLIB3S.LIB]
Evidence: module cstrt386 in CLIB3S.LIB publishes _cstart_@0x000, __exit@0x28f, __do_exit_with_msg__@0x292 and __GETDS@0x2cc in _TEXT; anchoring _cstart_ at 00043298 puts those at 00043527, 0004352a and 00043564, all real function starts here, and the module's code resumes at offset 0x78, which is this address. Corroborated by the runtime state it owns - the whole Watcom low-globals block at 0006041c-00060458 (initial ESP, PSP and environment selectors, DOS version, host type, NO87 flag, command line and program name pointers) - and by its callees __InitRtns (0004dfa6) and __CMain (0004df4c). Raw INT 21h/INT 31h probing and segment-register juggling with no C prologue rule out fdps; no AIL data or driver structures rule out ail; 535 bytes of real work rule out binary_artifact.
Name: no public symbol of its own. cstrt386 publishes nothing at offset 0x78, and being hand-written assembly it emits no LPUBDEF static name to recover, so the file-static form L$N_<module>_<purpose> applies, ordinal 1 as the module's only unnamed body ahead of the first public. No Function ID hit exists (0 candidates in both the Watcom and the ail sets).
Boundary: 00043310-00043526, ending at the CALL __CMain at 00043522, which never returns; the bytes at 00043527 are the module's public __exit. The entry proper is the 2-byte JMP at 00043298 that wears _cstart_, with the copyright data at 00043299-0004330f between it and this body.
Signature: no C convention. Hand-written assembly entered by JMP, never called; takes no stack arguments, cleans nothing up and never returns. The only incoming state read is loader-supplied: EDX (Intel Code Builder info block) and GS (DPMI selector). Any recorded void(void) prototype is a placeholder, assumed.

Algorithm:
  1. STI, align ESP down to a dword boundary, record the initial stack pointer
     at 00060434 and 00060420, preload selector 0x24 into 0006042c and EBX with
     'PHAR' for the Phar Lap probe.
  2. INT 21h AH=30h (get DOS version); AL/AH are stored as DOS major/minor at
     00060457/00060458. The high half of EAX selects the host:
       - 0x4458 ('DX'): Phar Lap 386|DOS-Extender. Version digit from BL; read
         the PSP memory-block end at ES:[5Ch] through selector 0006042c, round
         up to 4K, store at 00060420 and shrink the block with INT 21h AH=4Ah.
         Environment selector 0x2C.
       - 0x4243 ('CB'): Intel Code Builder. EDX points at the info block, saved
         at 000603ac; shrink memory by [EDX+1Ch] (INT 21h AH=4Ah), PSP pointer
         from [EDX+10h] (command tail at PSP+81h), environment segment from
         [PSP+2Ch] shifted left by 4.
       - otherwise: INT 21h AX=FF00h, DX=78h. If a host answers, this is the
         DPMI/DOS-4G path: a non-zero GS is saved at 000603b0, INT 31h AX=0006h
         fetches the DS segment base, the PSP selector comes from ES and the
         environment selector from ES:[2Ch]. If nothing answers, fall back to
         the fixed selectors (PSP 0x24, environment 0x2C, flat data 0x17).
     The host type/subtype pair goes to 0006044e/0006044f, the environment
     pointer to 00060451 and its selector to 00060455.
  3. Self-modifying step: with the flat data selector in ES, store DS into the
     code at 0004356d, the operand of the MOV DS,CS:[4356Dh] in the exit path.
  4. Command line: read the tail length from PSP:80h, skip leading spaces with
     REPE SCASB, copy the rest with REP MOVSB to the 16-byte aligned buffer
     past the end of BSS (0006a3bc rounded up), append two NUL bytes. That
     aligned buffer address is recomputed at the end and stored at 00060424,
     so 00060424 is the pointer to the copied command line.
  5. Environment scan: a string whose first four bytes lowercase to "no87" and
     whose fifth byte is '=' increments the no-x87 flag at 0006044c. After the
     terminating double NUL, skip the word count and copy the program name over
     the last NUL of the command line buffer; the address of that copy goes to
     00060428 and the first free byte past it to 00060430, the stack pointer to
     0006041c.
  6. Zero BSS from 00063930 to 0006a3bc with REP STOSD plus a byte tail; when
     the host type byte at 0006044e is 1 the cleared span is clamped to 0x1000
     bytes.
  7. CALL __InitRtns (0004dfa6) with EAX=0FFh to run every registered
     initializer up to priority 255, clear EBP, then CALL __CMain (0004df4c),
     which builds argc/argv, calls main and exits. __CMain does not return, so
     this call is the last instruction of the routine.
Open question: FD2 records the same vendor routine as one 557-byte function including the entry JMP and the copyright data; here it is split into _cstart_ at 00043298 and this body. That is an entity-layout difference only - both describe the same stock cstrt386 code, which is vendor-linked and not rebuilt from C.

=== 0004eba8 [PLATE]

It re-enables interrupts, PUSHADs the client's general registers to form the emulator's context block, then fills from the incoming trap frame the four fields it cannot take from its own registers, calls the emulator core at 0004ec3c, and restores DS/ES and the registers before IRETD.

Frame: the argument block handed to 0004ec3c is identical to the one __int7 at 0004ec18 hand-builds, which decodes every offset used here. PUSHAD lays down EAX..EDI; the two PUSHes add the ES and DS dwords on top; word [EBP-6] is the high half of the DS dword, exactly where __int7 stores SS (MOV word ptr [ESP+2],SS); and [EBP+0x0c] is the ESP slot of the PUSHAD block, exactly where __int7 stores the interrupted ESP. So the incoming frame holds, at entry ESP, +0x18 the interrupted ESP, +0x1c the interrupted SS (word), +0x20 ES and +0x24 DS, above the EIP/CS/EFLAGS that POPAD leaves ESP pointing at for the IRETD. These are values the extender's frame supplies because a ring-3 client's ESP and segments cannot be read out of the handler's own registers -- which is why this variant exists at all, and why the offsets reach past a plain same-privilege frame. The two pushed dwords do double duty: arguments to the core on the way in, and the values popped back into DS and ES on the way out.
Boundary: 0004eba8-0004ebc8, ends at the IRETD; the 3 bytes after it (87 db 90) are alignment padding before __int7_X32VM.
Signature: No C calling convention. Entered on vector 7, it reads nothing from EAX/EDX/EBX (all saved by PUSHAD, restored by POPAD), takes its inputs from the trap frame, and leaves via IRETD. The recorded __watcall(EAX, EDX, EBX) was Ghidra's guess and is not what the assembly does.

Resolves one POSIX TZ daylight-saving transition rule to a day-of-year for the given year: for rule form 0 (Mm.w.d) it calls __leapyear(year + 1900) to choose the leap or non-leap cumulative month-day table at 0x6385c / 0x63842, builds a struct tm for the first of the rule's month, calls mktime to obtain that day's weekday and yday, then advances to the w-th occurrence of the rule's weekday (w == 5 means the last one, falling back to the fourth when the fifth would run past the end of the month); rule form 1 (Jn) returns yday - 1 and any other form (n) returns yday unchanged.
Pool: crt  [library byte match against CLIB3S.LIB timeutil]
Evidence: The timeutil module of CLIB3S.LIB declares the local symbol calc_yday at _TEXT offset 0x39 in an LPUBDEF record, and the module's bytes there are identical to this body. The module's other symbols land on the image at one consistent base - __leapyear +0 -> 000523e5, calc_yday +0x39 -> 0005241e, check_order +0x12a -> 0005250f, __isindst +0x166 -> 0005254b, time_less +0x43e -> 00052823 - and the two public ones carry Function ID hits on timeutil.obj. The body corroborates it: named CRT callees __leapyear and mktime, tm_year converted to a Gregorian year by adding 1900, and the CRT's two 16-bit cumulative month-day tables read as dwords with SAR 0x10 to sign-extend the upper word, the difference of neighbouring entries being the length of the month.
Name: calc_yday - the library's own spelling, taken from the LPUBDEF record rather than invented. Function ID indexes PUBDEFs only, which is why a file-static shows no hit.
Boundary: 0005241e-0005250e, 241 bytes, matching the 0x39..0x12a span between calc_yday and check_order in the library module; four-register Watcom prologue at the entry, matching epilogue and RET at the end, empty gap before the next function.
Signature: __cdecl - the rule pointer at [ESP+4] and the year at [ESP+8] on entry, result in EAX, caller cleans up (plain RET, stack purge 0; check_order does add esp,0x8 after each call); the recorded __watcall int(void) was Ghidra's guess.
